title: Causes Behind Major Disruption to System at ICA Checkpoints on 31 March 2023
what_it_is: Causes Behind Major Disruption to System at ICA Checkpoints on 31 March 2023

sections.label: ICA checkpoint disruption questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Home Affairs about the causes, number affected, and lessons from the 31 March 2023 immigration system disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what are the main causes behind the major disruption to the immigration system at the ICA checkpoints on 31 March 2023; (b) how many people are affected by the disruption; and (c) what lessons can be learned from the disruption to prevent a future occurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the estimated number of people who were affected by the five-hour system disruption at the land and air checkpoints on 31 March 2023 arising from a scheduled system upgrade that caused a system overload; (b) why was the problem hitherto unanticipated; (c) what is the Ministry's assessment of the contingency plan activated to deal with the disruption; and (d) what steps will be taken to strengthen the plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what was the cause of the system breakdown which led to the long delays in clearance across all immigration checkpoints in Singapore on 31 March 2023; (b) how many people were affected by the delay; (c) whether the ICA has worked out a solution which will prevent similar breakdowns in the future or, if not, at least to ensure that the system will be restored in a much shorter time.

sections.label: ICA biometrics system trial
sections.summary: On 31 March 2023 at about 10.40 am, ICA was conducting a pre-scheduled trial for an upgrade of the Multi-Modal Biometrics System.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: On 31 March 2023, at about 10.40 am, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) was conducting a pre-scheduled trial needed for an upgrade of the Multi-Modal Biometrics System (MMBS).

sections.label: Land checkpoint delays
sections.summary: At the land checkpoints, travellers experienced delays of up to 30 minutes at the onset of the incident.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: At the land checkpoints, travellers experienced delays of up to 30 minutes at the onset of the incident.

sections.label: Passengers missed flights
sections.summary: Despite measures by ICA and CAG, 21 out of the 30,000 cleared passengers missed their flights at Terminal 4.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Despite the measures taken by ICA and CAG, 21 out of the 30,000 cleared passengers missed their flights at Terminal 4.

sections.label: Automated lanes resiliency enhancement
sections.summary: Resiliency of existing automated lanes not yet replaced by ABCS gates will be enhanced in the second half of 2023, though disruptions will still happen.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the meantime, the resiliency of existing automated lanes that have yet to be replaced by the ABCS gates will also be enhanced in the second half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Some of these capabilities will be implemented in a form and manner not used or tested elsewhere, as we customise them to suit our operational needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As such, while we will work closely with all stakeholders to further minimise technical disruptions and enhance system resiliency, the reality is, disruptions will still happen now and then.

sections.label: No data loss or mis-clearance
sections.summary: There was no loss or breach of data during the incident, and back-up processes minimised the risk of mis-clearance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And as the disruption lasted over close to five hours, were there any instances of mis-clearance at immigration or security concerns during the incident itself?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: There was no loss or breach of data during the incident.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With regard to mis-clearance, there were back-up processes in place, so that itself minimised the risk of mis-clearance.

sections.label: Checkpoint upgrading and disruption causes
sections.summary: The question asks why upgrading was not done at sea checkpoints first, and whether MHA investigated disruption causes and imposed liquidated damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, the question is that why did we not do the upgrading at the sea checkpoints first, rather than to do it straightaway at the busiest part of the Changi Airport, as well as the land checkpoints?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: And two, during the whole upgrading, did the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) check out what is the cause of these disruptions; and for the overloading of the database, if it was the fault of the contractors, are we imposing any liquidated damages?

sections.label: Travellers who missed flights
sections.summary: 21 travellers missed flights and were offered free rebooking within a week; 11 departed same day, four next day, two by land, two stayed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I have shared earlier, 21 travellers missed their flights, and these affected travellers were offered to rebook on alternative flights within a week at no extra cost.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Of the 21 passengers who had missed their flights, 11 passengers rebooked their flights and departed on the same day, four passengers rebooked their flights and departed the next day on 1 April 2023, while another two passengers departed by land and two passengers remained in Singapore.
